To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CDKN2B gene locus is associated with high levels of asbestos exposure in mesothelioma patients, and the expression of p16 is associated with high exposure to asbestos in the stroma.
CDKN2A copy numbers in tumor cells are associated with asbestos exposure and p16 immunoreactive stromal cells are more frequent in high exposure patients.

1) CDKN2A copy numbers in MPM tumor cell nuclei are associated with high asbestos fiber count; 2) stromal p16 expression is associated with high fiber count; 3) CDKN2As copy number is not associated with p16 expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between asbestos exposure and the genetic changes of CDKN2B and p16 expression.
a better understanding of the role of asbestos in the development of MPM.
the role of CDKN2 and its protein product p16 in MPM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the status of the CDKN gene locus and its expression in MPM is not clearly related to asbestos exposure.
the CDKN2As status and its corresponding protein expression in MPM tumor tissue is not associated with asbestos exposure.
CDKN2A alterations in MPM are not related to asbestos exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is no clear evidence for an association between the CDKN2AB gene copy number and the asbestos exposure status in MPM, although there are some hints that p16 expression in the tumor stroma may be associated with the asbestos exposure level in MPM.
there are some indications that asbestos exposure may affect the CDKN2B locus in MPM.
there is an association between high asbestos exposure levels and p16 immunoreaction in MPM stroma and an association between high exposure levels and CDKN2A copy numbers in MPM tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no evidence that the CDKN2As role in MPM is similar to that of lung cancer.
there are biological differences between the asbestos-associated mesotheliomas and the asbestos-associated lung cancer.
the association between p16 and asbestos exposure is not as straightforward as in the case of lung cancer.
